messages:
Emily W: quick heads-up, ran a focused quant mini-sweep on pioneer9b (fp32 / int6 / int4). want a short recommendation for GTN pilot vs full rollout.

Raj P: uploaded results to the bench link. high level: int6 looks like a safe compromise. int4 gives a large cost delta but shows regressions on long-context retrieval and some hallucination on multi-hop Qs.

Raj P: key table pasted:
```
model            p95_ms  tokens_per_s  $/1k_tokens  quality_delta_pct
pioneer9b-fp32    118     1750        $0.00058       +0.0
pioneer9b-int6    92      2100        $0.00039       -0.7
pioneer9b-int4    75      2550        $0.00020       -3.1
baseline-13b      112     1650        $0.00062       +0.0
```

Olivia B: added failures to the run. int4 failure modes: 1) higher hallucination rate on multi-hop retrievals, 2) ~0.8% cases truncated due to tokenization edge behavior, 3) KV-cache alignment drift for long contexts unless revalidation is applied. I attached representative inputs in the run.

Olivia B: example truncated case:
```
Input: "Describe implications of the 3rd/4th laws on irreversible processes and provide a short derivation..."
pioneer9b-int4 -> response cut off mid-derivation, missing concluding paragraph.
```

Drew L: ops note: int4 reduced peak GPU memory ~22% on A100 pools in our test, throughput gains as shown. but int4 artifacts require explicit KV-cache integrity checks on rolling restart. add to canary checklist.

Mariam C: product question: if we gate int4 behind a low-cost plan, what traffic fraction is safe for GTN pilot? also latency budgets for interactive product flows?

Raj P: my proposal for GTN pilot:
- Default GA model: pioneer9b-int6 (good balance)
- Low-cost/opt-in tier: pioneer9b-int4 but limited to single-turn or <200-token interactions and 15% of eligible traffic
- Immediate fallback: pioneer9b-fp32 if slice-level QA metrics breach thresholds

Raj P: suggested rollback triggers: MRR-equivalent quality delta > 1.2% on key slices OR hallucination rate > 1% on multi-hop QA slice.

Emily W: unit economics (back-of-envelope):
- int6 saves ~33% per 1k tokens vs fp32 -> ~$0.00019 saved per 1k
- int4 saves ~66% per 1k tokens vs fp32 -> ~$0.00038 saved per 1k
- For long-form retrieval flows (avg ~1k tokens) the -3.1% quality delta on int4 could cost more in conversion than the token savings. short chat (<150 tokens) looks fine on int4.

Drew L: scheduling: plan a small canary Fri 02:00 UTC with KV-cache checks and an automated rollback hook. we'll instrument token-level diffs and hallucination detector on the slice.

ProductBot: Feature request created -> ticket #4801: GTN pilot routing + rollback + telemetry.

BenchBot: full regression artifacts: https://bench.internal/runs/3626009999 (run id 3626009999). raw logs, diffs, and failing-samples tarball uploaded.

Mariam C: agree with cautious approach. product will sign off on an opt-in low-cost pilot (15% traffic cap, <200 token cap) and strict rollback. we'll monitor conversion and CSAT for 2 weeks.

Raj P: next actions: 1) eng-platform add routing flag + rollback thresholds (Drew). 2) eng-ml run 48h continuous slice-monitor and push nightly signals to the scorecard dashboard (Raj/Olivia). 3) product validates pricing and opt-in UX (Mariam).

Olivia B: starting the 48h continuous run now, will stream failure alerts to this thread. ping if you want access to raw traces.

Emily W: perfect. keeping this thread as the canonical short log. flag anything urgent into #incidents. :thumbsup:
